title: The Ventriloquist Illusion as a Tool to Study Multisensory Processing: An Update
review_question: To provide an update on recent advancements in understanding multisensory integration and learning using the ventriloquism effect and aftereffect, and to identify future research directions.

synthesis_conclusions: The ventriloquism effect and aftereffect are highly reliable experimental tools for studying basic mechanisms of multisensory integration and learning.
Recent research has revealed significant top-down influences from reward, motor systems, and mental imagery on cross-modal binding and learning.
Recalibration processes in the ventriloquism aftereffect operate at distinct immediate and cumulative time scales.
Neural mechanisms underlying multisensory integration and learning involve modulation of activity in auditory cortex and critical roles for parietal regions in causal inference and integration.
Neural oscillations play a crucial role in orchestrating stimulus-driven and top-down effects in multisensory processing.
evidence_gaps: Translating findings into a more general theoretical framework for multisensory processing in naturalistic environments.
Clarifying the developmental trajectory of short-term recalibration effects (VAE) and its relation to optimal cross-modal integration (VE) in humans.
Investigating the impact of sensory deprivation during sensitive periods of development on multisensory spatial functions in adult individuals.
Addressing how learned priors and sensory context interact with bottom-up sensory evidence in the brain.

limitations: Need for a more general theoretical framework for multisensory processing.
Limited research on multisensory processing in naturalistic environments.
Lack of studies on the ontogenetic development of multisensory spatial processing in humans.
Limited retrospective studies on the impact of sensory deprivation on multisensory spatial functions.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: The brain integrates multisensory information by inferring whether stimuli share a common cause, weighting sensory inputs based on their reliability, to produce a unified and optimal percept.
Sensory information from different modalities is combined in a statistically optimal manner to reduce perceptual uncertainty.

mechanism_chain.description: The ventriloquist illusion arises from the brain's attempt to integrate spatially disparate visual and auditory stimuli, often by inferring a common cause and weighting sensory inputs based on their reliability, leading to a biased perception of the auditory source towards the visual one.

steps.from_construct: Spatially disparate visual and auditory stimuli
steps.to_construct: Neural processing of multisensory input in sensory cortices
Shift in perceived auditory location (ventriloquism effect)

instruments_used.name: Auditory localization task
instruments_used.description: Behavioral task where participants indicate the perceived spatial origin of an auditory stimulus, often using a response device (e.g., mouse, joystick, button press) or verbal report.
